findings.claim: The philosopher David Hume called this the “inconsistent triad” — the three ideas seem to contradict each other. (repeated in the 12-mark mark scheme: “David Hume’s inconsistent triad”)
findings.truth: Hume never used the phrase. In Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion (1779) he restates Epicurus’s questions about God’s power, goodness and the existence of evil. The label ‘inconsistent triad’ belongs to the modern discussion of the logical problem of evil, associated with J. L. Mackie’s ‘Evil and Omnipotence’ (1955). Keep Hume as the philosopher a GCSE student names; drop the false coinage.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Problem of evil (Hume quoting Epicurus, no coinage credited to him); Wikipedia, J. L. Mackie. Same ruling applied to the free-tier twin unit on 6 Sep 2026.

Options: (a) merge the two lessons; (b) keep lesson 4 as sin and salvation and re-scope lesson 5 to the role of Christ in salvation — atonement in depth, with the theories and the contrasting Catholic and Protestant readings. Recommendation: (b). It keeps the 5-lesson shape and the existing narration for most of lesson 5, and it removes the duplicated opening. Tom’s call — it is a rebuild, not an edit.

findings.claim: “Nothing is impossible with God.” (Luke 1:37)
findings.truth: This is the 1984 NIV wording and is close to the NRSV (‘For nothing will be impossible with God’); the 2011 NIV reads ‘For no word from God will ever fail.’ It is the rendering every GCSE textbook uses, the reference is right and the speaker (Gabriel to Mary) is right. Leave it; changing it would break the matching card and the narration for no gain.
findings.evidence: Bible Gateway (NIV 2011 vs NIV 1984 / NRSV); same ruling on the free-tier twin unit

summary: Scripture in lessons 1-4 is verbatim NIV with the right references (Luke 1:37, John 3:16, 2 Thessalonians 1:6, Jeremiah 1:5, Matthew 28:19, Genesis 1:1-3, John 1:1-3, 1 Corinthians 15:17, Luke 23:43, Matthew 25:31-46, John 1:14, Matthew 3:17, Mark 9:7, Luke 22:42, Matthew 28:6, John 11:25, Acts 1:9, Romans 3:23, Romans 5:8, Ephesians 2:8-9, James 2:17, John 14:26, Isaiah 53:5), and every knowledge-check key and match order in the unit is correct. Lesson 5 is the weak one: John 3:16 and John 6:47 are paraphrased, 1 Corinthians 15:21 is transposed, a lesson-written definition is dressed as a quotation to learn, and the exam tip invents a 5-mark question. Across the unit: a misattributed coinage (Hume and the 'inconsistent triad'), the Nicene Creed quoted as 'right hand of God' instead of 'the Father', the board named in two lessons, banned board band names in all five 12-mark schemes and one exam tip, three 1-mark questions that demand two or three items, and one broken generator flashcard in every deck (including the mangled answer 'Jesusrsquos').
